persona.who: 25, Tamil-Singaporean analyst at a bank, first in family to go to university, got promoted early, feels she doesn't belong in the room.
persona.note: got promoted ahead of people with MBAs. in every meeting I think they're going to find out I'm just the girl from the HDB whose dad drove a taxi. I over prepare for everything and still feel sick before presenting

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call not feeling good enough, and that is where this week begins.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the dread of being found out, named without judgement.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the work you do is real and the one who does it belongs in the room.
week_beats.story: A woman who rose beyond her beginnings shows you what standing in your own truth looks like from the inside.

understanding.core_struggle: She was promoted ahead of more credentialed colleagues and now lives in fear of being exposed as a fraud, despite her preparation.
understanding.mirror: You overprepare and still feel sick before presenting, as if your preparation is not enough to prove you belong.
understanding.insight: The promotion is real and the work is yours. What keeps you sick is not the room but the story you tell yourself about who you are in it.

queries.hook: The dread of being found out, the overpreparation, and the feeling that the room knows something you do not. I feel like an imposter.
queries.diagnose: When the mind turns against itself, it treats a label as proof; self-blame grows from believing a story about who you are instead of what you do.
queries.steady: A title is given, not earned by pedigree; the work you do is real and the one who does it belongs in the room.
queries.act: Lift yourself up instead of pushing yourself down; speak the true thing about what you have done, and let your preparation be the answer.
queries.story: A woman who rose beyond her beginnings, faced the room that doubted her, and stood in her own truth until the room had to see her.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is standing on the battlefield, his hands trembling, and he tells Krishna that the mind is restless, stormy, powerful and stubborn. He says it is as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees that the mind is hard to hold. He says practice and letting go are what train it.
verse.for_you: You are in a room that is yours, yet your mind tells a story about the girl from HDB whose dad drove a taxi. The presentation is real, and the preparation is yours. Let the mind be stormy. Notice the storm without fighting it, and let the practice of returning to the work begin.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verse.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
verse.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.
verse.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free. Ashtavakra tells him that freedom is not a place you reach but a way you see yourself. He says that one who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verse.for_you: You are the girl from HDB whose father drove a taxi, and you are also the person who got promoted ahead of more credentialed colleagues. You have prepared for the presentation and the work is yours.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.
verse.translation: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.meaning: Vidura speaks to King Dhritarashtra, who is awake with worry the night before the peace talks. He tells the king that a wise person does not swell with praise or burn at a slight. They stay deep and still, like a river pool that is not disturbed by what flows above it. The verse proposes that you decide calmly, act steadily, and know what real happiness is made of.
verse.for_you: You prepared for this promotion and you earned it. When the room feels like it might expose you, let the work be the steady pool. Let the noise of praise and the fear of slight pass over it.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: I keep comparing myself to others

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is frozen by doubt. He tells Arjuna that it is better to walk your own path, even if you stumble, than to walk someone else's perfectly. Doing the work that fits your own nature, with all its flaws, is what matters. You do not incur any wrong by simply being who you are and doing what is yours.
verse.for_you: The work you do is real. You belong in that room. Let your own path be enough today.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Vidula speaks to her son Sanjaya, who has lost his kingdom and lies on the ground, defeated and despairing. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt, and not to settle for little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and to stop being afraid. She pulls him up and tells him to gather himself together.
verse.for_you: You got the promotion. That is real. Now gather yourself and set your mind on what is truly good in this work. Stop being afraid of the story you tell about yourself.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
verse.sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
verse.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
verse.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
verse.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, who is standing in a chariot between two armies, paralyzed by grief and confusion. Krishna is telling him that knowledge can cut through this darkness. He says to learn by bowing down, by questioning, and by serving those who have seen the truth. These wise people will teach you that knowledge, and it will carry even the heaviest wrongdoer across. The point is to trust the process of learning, to humble yourself enough to ask, and to cut through doubt so you can stand up and act.
verse.for_you: Your parents did not teach you to be perfect, they taught you to be diligent. Before your next presentation, ask one colleague how they prepared for a similar task, and listen to the answer without planning your reply. Let their method sit in your mind for a few minutes before you begin.

story.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
story.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
story.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
story.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

anchor.speaker: Jambavan
anchor.setting: On the southern shore no one can leap the ocean; old Jambavan turns to the silent Hanuman.
anchor.sanskrit: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।
anchor.line: You have the strength, the brains and the courage. Why are you holding yourself back?
anchor.translation: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
anchor.why: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

prasang.title: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is
prasang.summary: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone had named a number, and the one who could actually do it was sitting quietly at the back.
prasang.lesson: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.

story.hook_title: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.teaser: Everyone said how far they could leap, and Hanuman sat silent at the back
story.for_you: Stop measuring yourself against the others in the room. Stand in your own truth and take the step that is yours to take.

script: You are on the phone again. You are performing your life for your family, and the fear of being found out is eating at you. You are the girl from HDB whose dad drove a taxi, and now you are in a room that is yours.
On the battlefield, Arjuna is shaking. He tells Krishna that his mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

The mind is hard to hold. It will not sit still. It will tell you that you do not belong, that you are a fraud, that the promotion is a mistake. This is what the mind does. It is not your fault. Practice is not about stopping the storm. It is about returning to the work, again and again, without fighting the wind.
Before the presentation, the mind will tell you to run. Let it tell you. Then turn back to the work. That is the practice. Let the mind be stormy.

depth.life: You walk into your own office and your stomach tightens. The promotion is real, the work is yours, but the voice says you are still the girl from the HDB block. You overprepare until your hands shake, and then you stand there, performing for the room you have earned.
depth.points: The mind is not an enemy to defeat. It is a force that moves on its own. The story you tell yourself about who you are is not the truth of what you do. The work stands on its own, separate from the noise.
depth.practice: Sit with your phone in your pocket and let the anxious thought pass without answering it.
depth.question: What would it feel like to trust the work, not the story?
